name: Arrow sections with indented detail (Homebrew)
summary: Borrows from Homebrew: each step is a bold '==> label' arrow heading and its result is an indented detail line beneath, with git-style 'hint:' lines for next actions. A narrative top-to-bottom transcript, not a dashboard.

step_states: pending: not shown. running: the arrow heading is printed immediately in bold blue and a transient spinner sits on the line below it, replaced by the detail line. ok: detail line plain (heading turns bold green only in colour; no glyph needed). warn: detail line prefixed literal 'Warning:' in bold yellow. fail: prefixed literal 'Error:' in bold red. Prefix words, not colour, differentiate.
header: None; the first '==>' is the header. Optional '==> pkgdx init' root heading with steps as '  ->' children was rejected for noise.
success_summary: Final '==> Done in 2.9s' arrow line in bold green.
warning_presentation: Inline 'Warning:' line under the offending step and a 'hint:' line immediately after it (context stays adjacent). Closing arrow reports the warning count.
failure_presentation: Inline 'Error:' prefix, message on following indented line, 'hint:' line, then '==> Failed after 2 steps' in bold red. Output ends on the failure so BLUF holds for the reader at the bottom.
state_change_reporting: The indented detail line is the state report ('prek.toml updated', '.secrets.baseline created'); optionally make the changed noun bold.
non_tty_behaviour: Identical text with colour stripped; headings are only printed when the step starts, so a hung step is visible in a CI log. No spinner. Headings and details are one write each.
guidance_refs: standard-cli §4 brief and inform on change
risks: Roughly doubles the line count (12+ lines vs 6) which conflicts with 'keep it brief' in §4
Needs progressive-form labels ('Identifying...') instead of the existing imperative labels in _cli.py
Heading printed before the result means a warning appears after its heading, spreads one step across two lines
Ctrl-C needs a wrapper (print '==> Interrupted', exit 130)
curation_note: Homebrew style. Keep the existing imperative labels from _cli.py for headings (do not invent progressive forms). Its distinctive property is that the heading prints when a step STARTS, so a hung step is visible in a piped CI log - keep that.
